name: vs-glass
description: Glass optics for VS Code: a see-through window, refracting edges, specular rims and layered translucent planes, with density, tint, lens and aberration settings.

commands.title: Apply (write the glass effects into VS Code)
Remove (restore VS Code's original file and clean up)

vsGlass.effects.markdownDescription: Apply the glass effects (refracting rims, specular edges, near-clear planes) and, on macOS, the see-through window. VS Code has no extension point for either, so VS Glass adds one small, reversible hook to VS Code's own startup file (out/main.js, plus one splice in out/mainImpl.js on VS Code 1.141+); after one quit-and-reopen every VS Glass setting applies live. Reversible with **VS Glass: Remove**.

enumDescriptions: On macOS: make the window itself see-through (desktop blurred behind it). Elsewhere: off.
Keep an opaque window; the wallpaper backdrop is used instead.
vsGlass.windowTransparency.markdownDescription: See-through window (macOS only — Electron's vibrancy materials). `auto` and `on` make every workbench window transparent at creation and blend the desktop behind it with `#vsGlass.windowMaterial#`; `off` keeps a normal opaque window (the wallpaper addon then paints an in-page backdrop). Switches live once the hook runs; a newly created window picks the setting up at creation.

vsGlass.windowMaterial.markdownDescription: The macOS material behind the see-through window. `auto` (recommended) uses the system's `under-window` vibrancy: the window server blurs the desktop behind the window, which is what keeps code readable over any wallpaper. `none` turns the blur off, so the window shows the desktop unblurred. Applies live.

vsGlass.density.markdownDescription: How dense the work planes are — the editor card, the side bars, the panel and the activity bar — in percent: 0 is absolutely clear glass (only rims and text), 100 is the tuned default, 200 is opaque. The frame around them (title bar, status bar and the gaps between the planes) stays near-clear at every value. Floating widgets are separate (see `#vsGlass.widgetDensity#`). Applies live.

vsGlass.widgetDensity.markdownDescription: How dense and dark the floating widgets are (command palette, hovers, menus, notifications, dialogs, the Settings page) and the Claude Code composer, in percent. They keep a readable floor whatever the base density. Applies live.

vsGlass.tint.markdownDescription: A thin coloured film laid into every plane. `graphite` is a neutral grey that also adds legibility over bright desktops. Applies live.

vsGlass.lens.markdownDescription: How far the lens surfaces bend what is behind them — the minimap slider and the Claude Code composer (displacement and rim width scale together, so nothing folds). `extreme` turns them into magnifiers. Floating widgets are frosted glass and do not bend. Applies live.

vsGlass.aberration.markdownDescription: Chromatic aberration on the lens surfaces (the minimap slider and the Claude Code composer): red-to-blue fringing like a curved glass edge. `extreme` is a prism. Applies live.

enumDescriptions: Paint a neutral smoke backdrop only when the window is not see-through.
Always paint the smoke backdrop (opaque window look).
vsGlass.wallpaper.markdownDescription: The in-page backdrop for an opaque window: neutral smoke (no hue) that gives every rim something to bend. Applies live.

vsGlass.autoApply.markdownDescription: Re-apply automatically whenever a VS Glass setting changes (the change is live). Turn off to apply by hand with **VS Glass: Apply**.

scripts.audit: npm run audit:coverage && npm run audit:contrast
scripts.check: npm run build && npm run validate && npm run audit && npm run package
